_comment: LLM provider registry. Each provider maps to a response 'family' (the wire format the wiki knows how to build requests for and parse). Adding a new provider variant — e.g. a different endpoint that speaks one of the known families — is a JSON edit here, no code change. The three families (anthropic, openai-chat, openai-responses) are implemented in code (ai_core.php); only add a new 'family' value if you also add its parser. Fields: id (stored in each AI user's config), label (shown in Admin - AI - Provider), family, default_url (used when an AI user leaves the API URL blank).

providers.label: OpenAI / compatible — Chat Completions (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Ollama, …)

_comment_presets: Quick setup (the setup checklist's LLM Provider wizard): one card per service. Each is a preset for a provider above — 'provider' (its id), 'url' (the endpoint), 'model' (a suggestion the admin can change; model names go out of date, so review these), 'key_url' (where that service issues API keys) and 'no_key' for a local server that takes none. A service that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions format needs only a preset, no code.
_comment_model_rules: Per-MODEL request rules. The provider decides the wire format; the model decides which tuning parameters that format will accept, so these are matched separately. First matching 'match' pattern wins (case-insensitive regex, anchored patterns recommended); a model matching nothing gets the conservative defaults sampling=true, thinking=null, effort=false, reasoning_effort=false, i.e. exactly the pre-rules behaviour. Matching happens against the bare model name, after gateway prefixes and version tags are stripped (OpenRouter 'anthropic/claude-opus-5', Bedrock 'us.anthropic.claude-opus-5', Vertex 'claude-opus-5@2026...' all match '^claude-opus-5'). Patterns are prefixes, not exact names, so a point release inherits its predecessor's rules automatically — 'claude-sonnet-5-5' matches '^claude-sonnet-5'. That is why a new model in a known family usually needs no edit here; the longer names are listed anyway so the table says which models it has actually been checked against. The hazard is the same property: a future point release that needs DIFFERENT rules from its predecessor must get its own entry ABOVE the shorter pattern, or it will silently inherit the wrong ones. Fields: sampling (false = the model rejects temperature/top_p/top_k, so they are never sent), thinking ('adaptive' = Anthropic adaptive thinking, 'budget_tokens' = older fixed-budget extended thinking, null = the model cannot be asked to think), effort (supports output_config.effort), reasoning_effort (OpenAI reasoning_effort / responses reasoning.effort). Requests are also retried without a parameter the API rejects at runtime, so an unlisted model still works — the table just saves the wasted round trip.
